newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FOCUS - Dow Chemical plans to increase Asian presence.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dow Chemical plans to increase Asian presence.

text.p: The Dow Chemical Co plans to invest up to $300 million during the rest of the 1990s on various plans to expand its presence in Asia, chief executive officer William Stavropoulos said on Tuesday.
He outlined a series of projects being forged by the world's fifth largest chemical company for the booming Asia region, mostly focused in Southeast Asia, China and India.

Stavropoulos told a news conference sales from the company's Asian interest would grow over the next 10 years to 20 percent of global turnover from the current 13 percent. Dow's 1995 turnover was $20.2 billion.

"These sales will be supported by substantial increase in our Asia/Pacific production capacity," he said. "Currently, 27 percent of our sales in the regions are based on local production and we expect that number to approach 50 percent by 2005."
The U.S. firm is the world's largest producer of a number of chemical products, including polyethylene and polystyrene, used for packaging, caustic soda, a feedstock for producing PVC and chlorine.
The Asian projects included a newly announced 300,000-tonne-per-year joint venture polyethylene plant in Thailand with Siam Cement Co Plc, Dow said on Tuesday.
The $120 million venture was expected to come on stream in the first quarter of 1999 and will be called Siam Polyethylene Co Ltd, the company said.
The ethylene feedstock will be provided by a 600,000-tonne per year cracker owned by Rayong Olefins Co Ltd -- a consortium company led by Siam Cement.
Siam Polyethylene will own 22 percent of Rayong Olefins.

The company is also setting up a polyurethane plant in Guangzhou, southern China, geared to both domestic and export markets. Officials said Dow planned to upgrade a factory the company has acquired for the plant.
The company is also in talks with China's state-owned refining and petrochemical group SINOPEC to develop a petrochemical plant in Tianjin, northern China.
The project would include a 600,000-tonne-per-year naphtha cracker, Stavropoulos said, and a downstream petrochemicals plant.
In India, Dow has a number of small and medium-sized projects under way "to learn how to get things done and manage various relationships", he said.
He said the company was evaluating various options for Indian business and expected to make decisions in 1997 on more detailed plans.
